_about: What each townsperson says (NPC-01..14, AUD-03), generated by tools/voice/npc_lines.py.
roles: one per person (or kind of person). Each role is spoken in its 'voices' (designed voices from
('lines') and data/world/spawns.json ('lines' on a group) say which role a character speaks.
Events: greet (Rowan walks up), rumour (sometimes said instead of a greeting: points at a side
quest), startled (Rowan swings or casts close by), sword_drawn (instead of greet when his sword is out).
These are the 'before' lines (the prologue, NPC-01); the after-the-burying-ground and mending sets come later.
Townsfolk never name the Dreamlands (dialogue/bible.md). Keep lines short.

greet: Fence first, breakfast after. Same as every day.
That sword stays over the hearth. Your grandfather never could put an edge on it, and neither will you.
Shut the gate behind you. I mean it.
rumour: Something's been at the tallow in the cellar. Big, by the look of the teeth marks. Have a look, would you?
startled: Watch it! I've only the one good back left.
Put that down before you take my ear off.

nell.who: NPC-05 Nell Ashby, the dairymaid, at Oswin's barn

greet: You look like you slept in the hayloft. Again.
Daisy won't give a drop this morning. She keeps staring at the burying ground.
Do you ever dream about ships? Black ones, sailing on the clouds? ...Never mind.
rumour: There's scraping behind the barn walls at night. Rats, Oswin says. Rats don't sound like that.
startled: Rowan! You'll sour the milk swinging that about!
Oh! You great oaf, you nearly had my bucket over.

ebb.who: NPC-06 Old Ebb Harrow, the shepherd, with the herd

greet: Hmph. Counted them three times. Still two short.
Wolves don't leave tracks like that, lad. Nothing I've seen does.
Stay off the tor after dark. My father said so, and his father before him.
rumour: Two heifers gone from the high pasture. Footprints by the wall, big as a cartwheel. You go and look, if you've the stomach.
startled: Steady! You'll scatter the lot of them.
Not near the beasts, lad. Not near the beasts.

tam.who: NPC-07 Tam Corley, the smith's hand, by the smithy

greet: Can't sharpen that for you. Gerda does the fine work, and Gerda's not here.
Captain Thorne wants forty spearheads by midsummer. Forty! With what iron?
Ha! Mind the anvil, it bites.
rumour: Gerda went down the south road for iron three weeks back. Her cart never came home. I'd go myself, but somebody's got to keep the fire in.
startled: Whoa there! Save it for the goblins.
Ha! Not bad. Now point it somewhere else.

jory.who: NPC-08 Jory Matchett, the merchant, at the east stall

greet: Salt, pepper, good Hollin cloth. Last of it, so the price is what it is.
Two wagons I'm owed. The coast road's gone quiet, and nobody'll say why.
If you're ever down Saltmere way, ask after my brother. He'll stand you a drink.
rumour: My last wagon left the coast a fortnight ago. If you're on the south road, keep an eye out for a blue canvas. Goblins have been busy.
startled: Careful! That's my stock you're swinging at!
Easy, easy. Breakages are paid for.

maud.who: NPC-09 Granny Maud Pickering, the market seller, at the west stall

greet: Come here, dearie. Lavender for sleep? Everyone's buying it this month.
The Fletcher boy walks in his sleep now. Out to the burying ground and back. His mother ties his ankle to the bedpost.
Honey, herbs, a charm for luck. You look like you could use all three.
rumour: Lights on Brack Tor again. Green ones. I'm only saying.
There's an old man in the house on the hill who hasn't aged a day since I was a girl. Keep away from his gate, dearie.
startled: Mind my jars, you clumsy thing!
Gracious! At my age, a fright like that could finish me.

hester.who: NPC-10 Hester Lowe, the weaver, about the square

greet: Sit, sit. You'll be wanting to know about the hanging. Everyone does, eventually.
That's the knight who broke the Crown. See the sea behind him, and the mist? My grandmother said the cloth was older than the village.
The Watch wears through tabards faster than I can weave them. Green dye doesn't grow on trees, you know.
rumour: A panel's missing from the hanging. The last one. Nobody remembers what was on it, and I've asked everyone old enough to know.
startled: Not near the loom! Do you know how long that took?
Put that away this instant, Rowan Fenhallow.

greet: Morning. Mind the mud by the well, it's deeper than it looks.
Fine day for it. Shame about the wolves.
Barley's come in early this year. First good news in a while.
rumour: Goblins up past the east fields again. Took a whole fence for firewood, the cheek of them.
startled: Oi! Careful with that!
Watch where you're swinging!

greet: Oh, it's you! Mind the geese, they've taken against strangers this week.
If you're going out the north gate, be back before dark.
Good day to you. Off on some adventure, are we?
rumour: The baker swears she saw a man walking on the pond at dawn. On it, mind. Not in it.
startled: Gods above, put that away!
Whoa! Not near me, if you please!

pilgrims.who: NPC-12 travellers on the river road, walking to the waystone shrine

greet: Off to the waystone to pray for the harvest. Walk with us a while, if you like.
Blessings on you. The old stones still listen, whatever folk say.
rumour: The waystone was warm to the touch last time. Warm, at midnight. Make of that what you will.
startled: Peace, lad! We're only pilgrims!

bread_carrier.who: NPC-12 traveller on the east fields path, taking bread to the reapers

greet: Bread's still warm, if you're quick.
Reapers'll riot if this ale's late. Out of my way, dear.
rumour: The reapers won't work the far field any more. They say the crows won't land there either.
startled: Mind the basket!

tinker.who: NPC-12 traveller on the south-west lane, a tinker mending pots farm to farm

greet: Pots mended, knives ground, gossip free of charge.
Every farm on this lane owes me a supper. Good living, tinkering.
rumour: I've a scrap of old map, shows a tower in the Wolfwood nobody goes near. Yours for a few coins, if you're curious.
startled: Steady! I've nothing worth robbing!

washerwoman.who: NPC-12 traveller on the pond path, going to wash at the pond

greet: Washing day, every day. That's my lot.
If you see Oswin, tell him his shirts are on the hedge.
rumour: Something tangled my sheets at the bottom of the pond yesterday. Pulled, it did. I'm not going in after them.
startled: You'll have me in the pond!

greet: All quiet. For now.
Wolves on the east road again. Stay on the paths.
If you see goblins, you come and tell the Watch. Don't play the hero.
rumour: Corbin went out on the north-west lane two nights ago and hasn't come back. If you go that way, look for him.
sword_drawn: Keep your blade sheathed inside the fence.
Put that away, farmhand. There's nothing here to fight.
startled: Hey! Put that away before someone gets hurt.
Easy there! That's the Watch you're swinging at.

watch_patrol.who: NPC-14 the Watch patrol round the village

greet: Twice round the fence, she says. Twice! My boots are older than you.
Heard the Captain's sent for help from the Wolfwood garrison. Nobody's come.
rumour: Captain Thorne's paying for goblin ears and wolf pelts at the Watch house. Easy coin, if you've the stomach.
startled: Try that again and you'll spend the night in the stocks.
